text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we bumped into a weird case with prompt chaining + mixed precision. When a chain concatenates many short prompts (user -> tool -> assistant -> user), the KV cache ends up with tensors produced at different quant levels. Do we want the runtime to normalize caches to one precision or keep per-span precision?

jon: Interesting. My gut: normalizing to a single precision at boundary gives consistent quality but adds CPU/GPU conversion cost. Keeping per-span lets us save compute but complicates attention lookups.

kevin: Can we hybridize? e.g., keep per-span precision metadata, and at attention time do on-the-fly upcast when needed. That reduces conversions to only tokens referenced in the current window.

anya: Upcast-on-access sounds promising. But it's tricky for long-context where many tokens are repeatedly reaccessed — could re-upcast many times unless cached. Need an LRU or sticky upcast flag.

maria: Right. Proposal: runtime keeps KV entries with (precision, raw_bytes). We expose a small API: request.precision_hint (optional) per subrequest. Runtime behavior: if precision_hint matches stored precision, no conversion; else if hint is higher-precision, upcast-on-access and mark sticky until eviction; else if hint is lower-precision, serve by downcasting on the fly (and log quality regression).

jon: API question: how does the client set precision_hint for chained calls? Do we want the SDK to auto-propagate parent precision to child calls or force explicit opt-in?

kevin: For safety, default = inherit from root request. Apps that intentionally downgrade must opt-in per-call. Otherwise accidental quality loss in chains.

anya: Also telemetry must track cross-span degradation: record when downcasted tokens contribute to generation errors (perplexity/heuristic mismatch). We'll need a small calibration set that represents chained interactions.

maria: Agreed. Ops-wise: rollout plan — enable per-span metadata + sticky upcast in staging first. Add a canary to intercept chains and validate quality delta <= threshold (configurable). If > threshold, auto-fallback to unified precision for that session.

jon: Implementation detail: conversion kernels exist for fp8<->fp16 and int8<->fp16; 4-bit paths require special pack/unpack. We should add a conversion cost estimator to the scheduler so route decisions can include expected conversion overhead when deciding to pack chains onto the same device.

kevin: Also think about cross-tenant memory visibility — we must ensure per-tenant isolation of sticky-upcast flags and evictions. No cross-tenant caching leak.

anya: Edge-case: tool outputs (e.g., code completions) can be re-used by assistant prompts later. If tools run in a different precision tier (cheaper), the chain will see quality cliffs. We should include an op-level annotation: tool_outputs_allowed_precision = [fp8,int8] and runtime can auto-upgrade if downstream requests request higher precision.

maria: For the RFC follow-up doc I’ll add: API sketch, semantics for inherit/explicit-opt-in, sticky-upcast lifecycle, metrics to collect (per-token conversion counts, mean quality delta, session fallbacks), and rollout checklist.

jon: One more: add a small CLI test harness so QE can synthesize chained interactions with controlled prompts and measure degradation across precisions. That will speed validation.

kevin: I can prototype the upcast-on-access sticky cache in the runtime shim this week. I’ll open a draft PR and link tests.

maria: Awesome — please @kevin when you open it. I’ll write the RFC patch with the telemetry hooks and canary criteria.

quant-bot: deploy-checker: canary policy alert configured for staging: chain-degrade-threshold=0.015 perplexity_delta, sampling=1% :eyes:

anya: Nice, thanks. If we hit nontrivial regressions in staging we’ll run bisects with the CLI harness.

maria: Cool. Plan: kevin prototype -> jon add scheduler cost estimator -> maria patch RFC + telemetry -> canary rollout next week. Thanks everyone.
